items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: So I got the cornet, and so instead of being in the back line, I sat right next to Cohen.

ctx.x: I still hung around about two more weeks. So to get me off of his back, he called his favorite musicians out of the band, that would take care of the band in his absence. It was a Hebrew boy, he was like pretty well known academically. He was seeing and whatnot, all the boys, usually had something to do with all the boys on the ground, you know. And running errands for the teachers and things. He was mainly out of the Dean's office. He was a professional snitch, you know. He would let them know everything that…

So he says, "Cohen," he says, "let this kid use your horn." So the first number they pulled was "Caissans Go Marching Along." Says, "Give him your book." I says, "I don't need it." He looked at me. He gave a downbeat. I played it. "Semper Fidelis." I played it. "Anchors Aweigh." I played it. He says, "Hail to the Chief." I played it. Then he started getting easier: "Hail, Hail, the Gang's All Here," you know.
And then, that got him. So he says, "Come on in."
